body:
@sepo-agent /answer 

as our memory branch is gradually increasing in size, I wonder how the current sessions uses such memories -> how much memory has been loaded in each of the context? does it impact performance ?

comments.body:
I checked the current implementation. Short answer: the growing `agent/memory` branch is **not loaded wholesale into every model context**.

What happens today:

- `run-agent-task` resolves a memory mode, then only clones `agent/memory` if reads are enabled: [`run-agent-task/action.yml#L229-L246`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L229-L246).
- The clone is a shallow branch checkout into runner temp, not prompt injection: [`download-agent-memory/action.yml#L84-L88`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/download-agent-memory/action.yml#L84-L88).
- The prompt only injects `.github/prompts/_memory.md` when memory is available: [`run.ts#L176-L179`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/run.ts#L176-L179). That file is currently ~2.9 KB, roughly hundreds of tokens, not MBs.
- `_memory.md` tells the agent how to read memory selectively: `PROJECT.md`, `MEMORY.md`, relevant daily files, targeted `github/*.json`, or `memory/search.js`: [`_memory.md#L12-L16`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/_memory.md#L12-L16).

Current local memory size from this run:

| Area | Count / size |
|---|---:|
| Whole memory checkout | 228 files, ~3.5 MB file content / ~4.7 MB on disk |
| `github/*.json` mirror | 204 files, ~3.47 MB |
| `daily/*.md` | 15 files, ~10.8 KB |
| `PROJECT.md` + `MEMORY.md` + `README.md` | ~8.5 KB |
| Injected memory prompt fragment | 2,923 chars |

So the branch growth mostly affects **checkout size and ad hoc file/search reads**, not automatic context size.

Recent run examples from Action logs:

| Run | Memory mode | Rendered full prompt | Actual note |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Implement, May 11 | enabled | 18,428 chars | session resumed; actual sent prompt used continuation path |
| Review, May 10 | read-only for reviewer jobs | 23,588 chars | fresh review sessions |
| Review synthesis, May 10 | enabled | 20,967 chars | fresh synthesis session |
| Memory scan, May 11 | enabled | 11,642 chars | no persistent session |

Those `prompt_length` values are total rendered prompt chars, not just memory. They include base prompt, route prompt, request metadata, rubrics when selected, and the small memory instructions. The code logs this at [`run.ts#L334-L339`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/run.ts#L334-L339).

One important nuance: for resumed sessions, the runtime can send only a small continuation prompt instead of the full prompt. The adapter selects the continuation prompt when the session resume succeeds: [`acpx-adapter.ts#L246-L255`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/acpx-adapter.ts#L246-L255), wired from [`run.ts#L518-L528`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/run.ts#L518-L528).

Performance impact:

- **Model context/per-token cost:** small by default. Only `_memory.md` is injected automatically.
- **Runner I/O:** currently negligible at ~3.5 MB content. The shallow git pack is under 1 MB locally.
- **Search:** `memory/search.js` walks the tree on demand with defaults of 5 files and 3 snippets, and skips files over 512 KB: [`memory-search.ts#L34-L36`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/memory-search.ts#L34-L36), [`memory-search.ts#L193-L205`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/memory-search.ts#L193-L205). A local search here took ~0.13s.
- **Real risk:** an agent can still manually `cat` large JSON files, and those tool outputs do enter the session context. The prompt encourages targeted files/search, but there is no hard read budget yet.

I would recommend adding lightweight observability next:

1. Log memory checkout stats per run: file count, total bytes, `PROJECT.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `daily/`, `github/`.
2. Log injected memory prompt bytes separately from full prompt length.
3. Optionally add a `memory/summary` or `memory/stats` CLI so the agent can inspect size without dumping files.
4. Longer term, consider retention/compaction for old `github/*.json`, since that is the dominant growth source.

title: Review: how memory is used in recent PRs?
